def-knot-exterior:
## Definition

Assume countable choice, as required for the smooth normal-bundle structure in the tubular-neighbourhood interface. Let $K:S^1\to S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $\nu(K)=TS^3|_K/TK$ be its quotient normal bundle, and let $\Phi:\Omega\to S^3$ be a tubular-neighbourhood map from an open neighbourhood $\Omega$ of the zero section in $\nu(K)$ that restricts to the inclusion of $K$. Choose a radius $\epsilon>0$ whose closed disk subbundle $D_\epsilon\nu(K)$ is contained in $\Omega$, and set $N(K)=\Phi(D_\epsilon\nu(K))$. The **exterior** of this chosen tube is
$$
E_K:=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}_{S^3}N(K).
$$
Retain its boundary $T_K:=\partial E_K=\partial N(K)$, orient $E_K$ by restriction of the fixed orientation of $S^3$, and orient $T_K$ as the boundary of $E_K$. The choice of tubular map and radius is part of the input to this definition.
lem-knot-normal-circle-bundle-trivializa:
## Statement

For every smooth oriented embedding $K:S^1	o S^3$, let $
u_K=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$ be the quotient normal bundle. Orient its two-dimensional fibres so that a positive tangent to $K$ followed by a positive basis of the normal fibre gives the fixed orientation of $S^3$. Then $
u_K$ admits a smooth orientation-preserving bundle isomorphism $
u_K\cong K	imes\mathbb R^2$.
def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitud:
## Definition

Assume countable choice as in the chosen tubular-neighbourhood data. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot with chosen exterior $E_K$ and boundary torus $T_K=\partial E_K$, and let $p:T_K\to K$ be the projection of the chosen normal-disk tube. Orient each normal disk so that its positive tangent direction followed by its oriented normal basis agrees with the orientation of $S^3$. A **meridian** $\mu$ is the oriented boundary of one such normal disk. A **degree-one parallel curve** is a simple closed curve $\lambda$ in $T_K$ for which $p|_\lambda:\lambda\to K$ has degree $+1$. A **preferred longitude** is a degree-one parallel curve satisfying $i_*[\lambda]=0$ in $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$, where $i:T_K\hookrightarrow E_K$ is inclusion. This is a condition on a curve; this definition alone asserts neither existence nor uniqueness. Reversing the orientation of $K$ reverses the orientations of both $\mu$ and any degree-one parallel curve. If a subgroup $P\le\pi_1(E_K,x)$ is specified using a path from $x$ to $T_K$, record it only up to replacing it by $gPg^{-1}$ for $g\in\pi_1(E_K,x)$.
lem-knot-tubular-exterior-and-boundary:
## Statement

Assume countable choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in $S^3$, there are an oriented normal-bundle trivialization, a tubular map $\Phi$ defined on an open neighbourhood containing $S^1\times D^2_{2\epsilon}$ for some $\epsilon>0$, and a closed tubular neighbourhood $N(K)=\Phi(S^1\times D^2_\epsilon)$. This $N(K)$ is diffeomorphic to $S^1\times D^2$, its boundary $T_K$ is diffeomorphic to $S^1\times S^1$, and its exterior $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ is a compact smooth oriented three-manifold with boundary $T_K$. The open complement $S^3\setminus K$ strongly deformation retracts onto $E_K$.
lem-knot-exterior-has-peripheral-torus:
## Statement

Assume countable choice. For a smooth oriented knot with a chosen product tubular neighbourhood $N(K)\cong S^1\times D^2$, let $\mu$ be the positive fibre meridian and let $\sigma$ be the product section $s\mapsto(s,1)$ of $T_K=\partial N(K)\cong S^1\times S^1$. Then $T_K=\partial E_K$ is a torus and $[\mu],[\sigma]$ form a basis of $H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)$. The curve $\sigma$ is a product section; this statement does not assert that it is the preferred zero-homology longitude.
thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K:S^1	o S^3$ be a smooth oriented embedding and write its quotient normal bundle as $
u_K=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$. Choose an orientation-preserving trivialization $
u_K\cong S^1	imes\mathbb R^2$ and a tubular map $\Phi:\Omega	o S^3$, meaning a smooth embedding from an open neighbourhood $\Omega\subseteq
u_K$ of the zero section onto an open neighbourhood of $K(S^1)$ with $\Phi(s,0)=K(s)$, such that in these product coordinates $\Omega$ contains $S^1	imes D^2_{2\epsilon}$ for some $\epsilon>0$. Here $D^2_r=\{z\in\mathbb R^2:\|z\|\le r\}$. Set $N(K)=\Phi(S^1	imes D^2_\epsilon)$, $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$, $T_K=\partial E_K$, and let $i:T_K\hookrightarrow E_K$ be inclusion, $p:T_K	o S^1$ the product projection, and $\mu$ the positive boundary of a normal disk, using the normal-plane orientation determined by the orientations of $K$ and $S^3$. A class is primitive if it is not $m$ times another class for any integer $|m|>1$. Then $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ is generated by $[\mu]$. The kernel of $i_*:H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)	o H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$ is a primitive rank-one direct summand generated by a unique class $[\lambda]$ with $p_*[\lambda]=1\in H_1(S^1;\mathbb Z)$. It has a simple closed representative, is the preferred longitude, and $([\mu],[\lambda])$ is a basis of $H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)$.
